text:
Ridly Greig leads the NHL in penalties drawn, by a lot: 21, per North State Journal's Cory Lavalette, when second place had 15. That is the most Ridly Greig stat imaginable. NHL.com asked whether he has become a shutdown specialist, and his usage says yes: up to almost 19 minutes a night since William Eklund went down.

The scoring hasn't followed. Three goals on 5.1 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), six points in 20 games, though Ottawa has also scored more goals than its chances with him on. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that his teammates were strong enough to flatter his raw numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking likes him in two places: 62% of his exits leave the zone with possession, and he gets to the dangerous ice in front of the net more than most forwards. He is the kind of player opponents hate and Senators fans love, on a team that has points in eight straight. Our range has him around 16 goals.
